title: Terms of Change on a Firm Resort Lodging Reservation
content:
A firm Resort Lodging reservation may be changed in its dates, its unit type or the size of its party.

A change is accepted only when it is recorded on or before the unit type's change deadline, which is its change notice period counted back in calendar days from the arrival date. Calendar days are counted back from the arrival date, the arrival date itself counting as day zero, every day of the week counting alike, and a calendar day is never mixed with a full 24-hour period; the deadline is the day the count lands on, and where that day does not exist in the target month the last day of that month is used. The arrival date is taken from the collective's own reservation record, and a change recorded on the deadline day itself is within the period.

Each change carries the unit type's change fee, whatever the direction of the change.

Nights added to a stay are priced on the rate window each new night falls in at the rate published on the day of the change, and nights taken off are credited at the rate they were booked at.

A change that takes the stay below the minimum nights of the window it now falls in is refused, and the household is offered a cancellation instead.

A reservation may be re-registered to a different lead guest where the unit type allows it, against the unit type's re-registration fee.

A fee is posted to a folio only while the reservation stands as awaiting its deposit, firm, checked in, checked out, given up or unclaimed.

### The deadline at its two edges (a hypothetical unit type whose change notice period is 10 calendar days)

An arrival date of the 20th of February makes the 20th day zero; counting back 10 calendar days lands on the 10th of February, which is the deadline. A change recorded on the 10th of February is recorded on the deadline and is accepted. A change recorded on the 11th of February falls after the deadline and is not.

### Pricing a change in both directions

A stay lengthened by two nights is priced on the rate window each of those two new nights falls in, at the rate published on the day the change is recorded rather than the rate that stood at booking. A stay shortened by two nights is credited at the rate those two nights were booked at. Either way the unit type's change fee is carried, because the fee attaches to the change and not to its direction.
